main_issue: Source Data table corrupt on deposit
finding: Figure 4, base against fine-tuned model, 260 protein-organism pairs: Jaccard 0.7379 against 0.74 published, codon similarity 69.2629% against 69.26%, normalized DTW 0.0459 ± 0.0338 against 0.05 ± 0.03. The released checkpoints regenerate all 520 benchmark sequences byte for byte. An independent blind rerun got the same numbers to every digit and a different label, because the two runs set different bands: ours asked for 1e-6 agreement on each of 260 DTW values and got none, which fails our own frozen rule, while the blind run put its band on the means alone and passes. We publish both and name the bad band as ours. Three defects in the release: the per-pair DTW table of the Source Data carries one value per protein under every pair label, found independently by both runs; equation 6 of the Methods does not describe the %MinMax that was computed, which is the Clarke & Clark statistic the cited R package implements; and the base checkpoint repository ships no tokenizer. The paper's own figure is fine.

From the released chains, no re-sampling: the HD amplitude at gamma = 13/3 comes out at 2.4039 (+0.665/−0.589) × 10⁻¹⁵, the authors' own stored output to the digit, and the thermodynamic-integration Bayes factors give log10 BF 12.11 (CURN vs IRN) and 14.41 (HD vs IRN), inside the published ranges. The chain behind the headline number was removed from the repository in 2024 and survives only in its git history and on Google Drive. Two smaller points: the presampled HD vs CURN core is a fixed-gamma run, not the varied-gamma comparison of Fig. 2, and the TI quadrature moves log10 BF by 0.3, more than the quoted ±0.1. An independent blind rerun got the same numbers.

Flat ΛCDM from the public DR1 BAO distances, our own likelihood with CAMB: Omega_m = 0.2947 ± 0.0146 against 0.295 ± 0.015 and r_d h = 101.90 ± 1.27 Mpc against 101.8 ± 1.3. H0 with BBN comes out at 68.69 ± 0.81 against 68.53 ± 0.80, 0.2σ high and just outside our band. The cause is in the authors' own chain: Section 2.4.1 gives the ΛCDM BBN prior as Eq. (2.8), but the chain behind the published H0 uses the ΛCDM+N_eff prior evaluated at N_eff = 3.044, which shifts the mean down by 0.37σ. Their chain that does use Eq. (2.8) gives 68.67, like ours. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values and found the same prior on its own.

main_issue: Test lists or evaluation commands not published
finding: Fig. 2b with the released weights: median ROC AUC 0.9247 against 0.92 on the 53 MaSIF-site subunits, and all 53 match the authors' own notebook outputs to three decimals. On the 417-structure ScanNet set, 0.9299 against 0.93, with 415 of 416 structures matching the Source Data to 0.001. Neither the benchmark dataset file nor the ScanNet structure list is in the repo, so we rebuilt both. Two entries drifted with PDB revisions: 4DX0 gives 0.961 instead of 0.909, and 1FSS now exceeds the code’s atom limit and drops out. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values.

main_issue: Released checkpoints differ from the paper
finding: Table 3 (scaffold splits) with the published fine-tuned weights: BBBP 0.8913 against 0.902, BACE 0.7104 against 0.832, Tox21 0.6131 against 0.653, SIDER 0.7180 against 0.745, and no model is published for the HIV column. Our validation run matches the authors' own TensorBoard logs, which ship inside the model folders, bit for bit on three metrics per task, so the split, the metric and the weights are theirs. The published scaffold training command also crashes as released, on the line that prints the number. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values.

Fig. 1 (global RMSE, 2020) for IFS HRES, GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, the two operational-start rows and NeuralGCM 0.7°: all 50 pre-registered Z500 and T850 cells match on the full 732 initialisations. Z500 matches with the public code as it is; T850 only matches with the below-ground mask of Section 4.2.1, which is not in the public code. We pointed the authors to it.

main_issue: Settings behind one result not published
finding: Power Law + Peak run, rerun twice from the released event arrays and injections: mass peak 33.5-33.6 Msun (paper 34 +2.6/-4.0) and BBH rate at z=0.2 of 28.3-28.4 Gpc^-3 yr^-1 (paper 28.3 +13.9/-9.1). The rate step reuses a stale spin shape, which moves the median by about 0.13, and the example config differs from the published run.

Table 1 (compleasm rows) with the v0.2.2 release: six of seven genomes agree within 0.3 points on every category. Maize gives 99.4% complete against 96.7% with today's BUSCO odb10 lineage, re-released in 2024. With the 2020 lineage the author sent us, maize matches too: 96.72 complete, 82.23 single, 14.49 duplicated, 3.03 fragmented. v0.2.2 also crashes on today's lineage index.

main_issue: Released checkpoints differ from the paper
finding: 2022 tables with the 2022 data and checkpoints: 21 of 26 nRMSE values match at the printed 2 significant figures, including all 10 Darcy Flow values. The released 2022 Advection β=1.0 FNO checkpoint behaves like a β=0.4 model (nRMSE 0.63 against 5.9e-03), and three Burgers FNOs come out 1-9% lower. We told the authors.

Fig. 2B (AFDB clusters): on the 32 clusters whose inputs are still complete, 31 give the authors' LDDT to 6 decimals and the same alignment. 285 of the 3,200 benchmark structures have since been deleted from AlphaFold DB, so the 160-cluster means run on reduced inputs only. Fig. 2A could not run: the HOMSTRAD reference is offline and not archived anywhere we could find.

Fig. 4 (ligand-receptor methods scored against spatial co-localisation on 5 Slide-tags datasets) re-runs from the released files and matches the Source Data to about 1e-16. In the evaluation code, the FDR correction the Methods describe is applied to a 0/1 vector and has no effect; done as described, it reorders the methods. We asked which was intended.

main_issue: Settings behind one result not published
finding: Table 3 with the released distances and covariance: Omega_m = 0.3327 ± 0.018 against 0.334 ± 0.018 in flat ΛCDM; the ΛCDM and wCDM rows and the SH0ES H0 (73.54 against 73.6) also hold. The w0waCDM row does not (Omega_m 0.32 against 0.403); it depends on the prior range, and the authors' released chains do not reach 0.403 either. We asked which prior and settings produced it.

Table 1 with the released checkpoints on all 20 M JetClass test jets: ParT accuracy 0.86051 and AUC 0.98772 match the printed 0.861 and 0.9877, and all nine background rejections fall inside the pre-registered statistical band; all 11 ParticleNet numbers match. The README installs weaver-core>=0.4, which now gives 0.5.3; with it the same checkpoint runs without error but scores 0.123 accuracy.

main_issue: Test lists or evaluation commands not published
finding: Table 1 (protein-to-genome alignment accuracy of miniprot-0.7): % confirmed splice junctions matches in all four columns, but base-level sensitivity on the human genome comes out 0.95 to 1.2 points lower and 6 of 12 percentages miss the 0.5-point tolerance. The paper does not publish the test protein lists or the evaluation command lines; we asked the author for both.

Fig. 4 (COMP6 energy and force errors of three released ML potentials) does not reproduce: 3 of 36 values match, the rest differ in both directions. Two independent runs of ours agree with each other within 0.03 meV/atom. The model ranking holds. We asked the authors how the figure was computed.

All five headline numbers (ESM-1b and four ESM2 sizes) match within 0.003 over all 217 assays, confirmed by a second, independent run. The paper's averages come from the script's protein-first grouping, not the text's definition; ESM-1b was scored with wt-marginals, not the masked-marginals the appendix states; and five long-protein ESM2 scores were computed on the MSA region only, unlike the released code.

The main claim holds: atomic context raises recovery near ligands, most near metals. Three of six headline numbers match. The authors' own per-protein data show that the figure used a different neighbourhood definition than the Results text, and metal-only context on the metal split; that choice moves the metal number by about 15 points.

main_issue: New dependency release breaks the code
finding: All targets within 0.1σ, chains run to the paper's convergence criterion. The released setup no longer runs on CAMB 2.x; CAMB 1.3.6 works.
The released model behaves as described, but the test split was drawn without a fixed seed and never published, so the headline test error can't be re-checked.
All 46 values on real microscopy data match within 0.01. The noisy test images behind the main benchmark were never released.

main_issue: More compute than one home GPU
finding: All four values fall inside our 95% interval on a weighted 300k-window sample. The full test set would take about 115 days on our GPU.
